prompt: An order-events producer added an optional field and deployed successfully, but one older consumer now rejects every message, backlog rises, and producer retries increase. Diagnose and recover without deleting messages or forcing every team to upgrade at once.
directAnswer: Bind topic or channel, event type, producer version, schema identity, affected consumer group, first rejected offset or delivery, error class and backlog age. The producer change may be backward-compatible for tolerant consumers but forward-incompatible with a consumer that rejects unknown fields. Pause or isolate the failing rollout or consumer according to ownership, stop retry amplification, preserve the log and replay position, and prove whether unaffected groups continue. Restore compatibility by making the consumer tolerate documented unknown optional fields or by using a separately versioned contract and migration path. Test old/new producer-consumer matrices, replay the quarantined cohort from the preserved position, verify one business effect per event, backlog drain, no gaps or duplicates, and record the consumer behavior that made an additive schema change breaking.
foundation: Compatibility is a relationship between producer, contract and actual consumers. Adding an optional field is not universally safe when an existing consumer rejects unknown data.
reasoningSteps: Bind event identity, contract version, producer and consumer versions.
Preserve offset, backlog and rejected payload evidence without sensitive data.
Separate schema description from actual consumer behavior.
Choose rollback, tolerant consumer repair or explicit version migration.
Replay from a preserved point with durable duplicate control.
Verify business effects, gaps, duplicates and backlog drain.
seniorAnswer: I preserve the log and consumer position, contain the incompatible cohort and test actual old/new wire behavior. I do not delete the message, skip the offset silently or label the field additive and blame the consumer; the supported compatibility contract must describe unknown-field behavior.
weakAnswer: Optional fields are always backward compatible, so increase retries until the consumer catches up.
whyWeak: The old consumer is demonstrably strict; retries reproduce the same poison message, amplify load and do not create compatibility.

evidence.signal: producer version contract identity consumer version and rejection
offset or delivery ID and backlog age

followUps.prompt: Why not skip the poison message?
followUps.answer: Skipping can create a silent business gap and may violate ordering; quarantine requires explicit policy, ownership, reconciliation and later replay or compensation.

followUps.prompt: Is a new event type better than a version field?
followUps.answer: It can make semantics explicit, but creates parallel lifecycle and migration work. Choose from consumer independence and meaning, not naming preference.
Consumer failure and age/backlog against the business delay objective, correlated with contract and deployment version.
